entities.name: Lysophosphatidylserine
observations: Macrophage effects vary by lipid chain length, inflammatory state, dose, and signaling route; it can increase cholesterol loading while also reducing selected inflammatory responses.

entities.name: Atherosclerosis
observations: Retrieved evidence supports macrophage-level opposing effects of lysoPS, but does not establish altered plaque development, stability, or regression in vivo.

entities.name: LysoPS foam-cell effect
observations: In RAW264.7 and mouse peritoneal macrophages, lysoPS increased oxLDL-associated cholesterol accumulation and CD36, MSR1, LOX1, and TLR4 expression, consistent with increased foam-cell propensity; plaque effects were not tested.

entities.name: LysoPS resolution effect
observations: In acute inflammatory models, neutrophil-associated lysoPS signaling through macrophage G2A enhanced efferocytosis and resolution-associated macrophage responses; this is not direct evidence of atherosclerotic plaque benefit.

entities.name: LysoPS species-dependent signaling
observations: Very-long-chain lysoPS induced TLR2-dependent pro-inflammatory macrophage responses, while long-chain species engaged TLR2-independent signaling, indicating chain-length-dependent outputs.
